title: Decoding Big Trades: What Are Block Deals and Bulk Deals?
description: Block Deals** are very large, pre-arranged stock trades (at least ₹25 crore or 5 lakh shares) done in a special, separate window to avoid sudden price changes.

faq.q: Where can I see details of bulk and block deals?
faq.a: You can find these details on the official websites of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) after market hours each day. They usually have dedicated sections for "Bulk Deals" and "Block Deals".

faq.q: Do block deals affect the stock price?
faq.a: Block deals are specifically designed to minimize immediate price impact because they happen in a separate, pre-arranged window outside the live market. However, the public disclosure of a large block deal after market hours can influence market sentiment and the stock's price on subsequent trading days.

faq.q: What kind of investors typically participate in these deals?
faq.a: Mainly institutional investors like mutual funds, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), insurance companies, pension funds, and high-net-worth individuals (HNIs) participate in both bulk and block deals.

faq.q: Is there a minimum value for a bulk deal?
faq.a: While some older references might mention a value, the primary definition for a bulk deal by SEBI is based on quantity: buying or selling more than 0.5% of a company's total listed equity shares in a day.
